subject: Proposal: tiered-year bridge with seasonal burst carve-outs + opt-in auto-extend
messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Mendez <amendez@skylinehealth.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Proposal: tiered-year bridge with seasonal burst carve-outs + opt-in auto-extend

Hi Alicia —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Per our discussion I attached a compact proposal with two structure options that are designed to align Skyline's fiscal seasonality and give you runway to scale this year: a 24-month bridge with a front-loaded ramp, and a 36-month ladder with graduated discounts. Key highlights: 

- Seasonal burst carve-outs: we reserve an agreed quarterly burst pool (measured in token-hours) that does not count toward the committed bucket when used during specified "high season" windows.
- Ramp schedule (24mo option): 0–6mo 40% commit, 6–12mo 70% commit, 12–24mo full commit; credits issued for underutilization in the onboarding window.
- Auto-extend (opt-in): a one-time optional 12-month auto-extend that Skyline can elect at month 20; electing the auto-extend locks current pricing and provides a 4% discount on year 3 pricing.
- Co-terming: we can co-term additional regional subscriptions to the master contract within a 90-day window at signing.

I attached: 20260720_Skyline_Renewal_Proposal.pdf and a sample milestone schedule (example_milestone_schedule.xlsx).

Next steps I propose:
1) You and procurement review; send any redlines to this thread.
2) If the 24mo bridge looks closest, Lauren will send a clean redline with the ramp credit mechanics.
3) If procurement wants a finance-friendly cadence we can flip billing to quarterly upfront with an escrow-style burst reserve.

If helpful I can set a quick 30-min call with Camila (CS lead) to run through the operational implications of the burst carve-out.

Thanks,

Markus Klein
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
markus_klein@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments: 20260720_Skyline_Renewal_Proposal.pdf (application/pdf), example_milestone_schedule.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Alicia Mendez <amendez@skylinehealth.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Cc: Skyline Health Procurement <procurement@skylinehealth.com>, Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 13:45:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Proposal: tiered-year bridge with seasonal burst carve-outs + opt-in auto-extend

Markus —

Appreciate the clear options and the sample schedule. A few quick questions from procurement and finance: 

1) How does the burst carve-out get reconciled on invoices? Do we track usage separately or do you issue credits after each quarter?
2) If we elect the auto-extend at month 20, is there any proration on unused burst capacity?
3) Our finance team prefers a monthly billing cadence; can you confirm whether switching to monthly changes the discounting or credit calculations?

Procurement is looping in a couple people on this thread. Camila, can you confirm operational impact for the burst carve-out?

Thanks — Alicia
Alicia Mendez
Director, Cloud Platforms
Skyline Health
amendez@skylinehealth.com

Cc: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 08:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposal: tiered-year bridge with seasonal burst carve-outs + opt-in auto-extend

Alicia / Markus / Camila —

Quick note on structure options from a pricing standpoint. If Skyline needs the most cost predictability with a finance-friendly cadence, consider this hybrid we use often: a 36-month ladder where years 1–2 have a lower minimum commitment and year 3 is a committed uplift, paired with an annual true-up and an upfront credit applied to year 1 to offset onboarding friction. Benefits: preserves unit economics for Redwood while giving Skyline predictable per-token effective pricing.

Suggested fiscal-friendly changes:
- Billing cadence: quarterly upfront (preferred) or monthly net 30 (acceptable) with a small processing uplift if monthly.
- Burst reconciliation: we reconcile burst usage at quarter close and issue credits on the next invoice as an "onboarding/burst adjustment" line item.
- Auto-extend: make the auto-extend election a signed amendment; proration of burst is handled by converting remaining burst hours to a credit at the same unit rate.

I've attached a quick model (36mo_fin_model.xlsx) that maps the ladder and the effective blended unit price across ramp scenarios.

Happy to hop on a call to walk through numbers.

—Lauren
Senior Account Manager, Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.com

Attachments: 36mo_fin_model.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Mendez <amendez@skylinehealth.com>, Skyline Health Procurement <procurement@skylinehealth.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Jul 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposal: tiered-year bridge with seasonal burst carve-outs + opt-in auto-extend

Alicia / team —

Thanks for the questions; summarizing a compromise that should address procurement and finance preferences: 

1) Structure: We propose the 24-month bridge as the default with a 12-month optional extension election at month 20 (the "opt-in auto-extend"). If you elect extension the extension becomes a signed amendment with locked pricing and a 4% year-on-year discount for the extension term.
2) Burst reconciliation: Reed (finance) will reconcile burst at quarter close; any overage in the burst pool will be converted to a credit on the following invoice. If Skyline prefers invoice-level line items, we can show the burst adjustment as a separate credit line.
3) Billing cadence: we can support monthly net 30 without changing the ramp credit mechanics; there is a 0.5% processing uplift applied to monthly billing to cover increased settlement frequency (we can waive this for enterprise agreements > $X).
4) Co-terming: additions from other Skyline regions can be co-termed within a 90-day window of the master signature and will inherit the ramp schedule pro rata.

Next steps:
- Procurement: please confirm if quarterly vs monthly is a hard requirement. If monthly is required, let us know and we'll produce a cost schedule with the uplift line item.
- Legal: if procurement can share any preferred redlines, we will produce a clean amendment.

I'll prepare a DocuSign packet for the 24mo bridge + optional 12mo extension and send it once we get procurement's go-ahead.

Best,

Markus
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
markus_klein@redwood.com

Related link: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/23914

From: Alicia Mendez <amendez@skylinehealth.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Skyline Health Procurement <procurement@skylinehealth.com>, Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Jul 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposal: tiered-year bridge with seasonal burst carve-outs + opt-in auto-extend

Markus / Lauren —

Thanks — this summary is helpful and aligns with what procurement needs. We are comfortable proceeding with the 24-month bridge + optional 12-month extension language provided: 

- Burst reconciliation shows up as a quarterly credit line (that works for our ledger).
- Monthly billing is acceptable; procurement will accept the 0.5% processing uplift for our pilot (we prefer monthly cashflow).
- One legal redline: in Section 4.2 we need clearer language around data residency for burst logs and audit retention (SOC2 evidence). Can your legal team add standard Residency & Retention language?

If you can add the data residency bullet and include the DocuSign link we can get procurement to sign this week.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Alicia
